formationLabel: Organized as a Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish in 1906 · cornerstone 18 August 1907 · Lithuanian national-parish identity broadened through the 1973 territorial consolidation · closed 31 December 1989
currentUse: The parish ended on December 31, 1989. A current nonprofit directory associates Universal Community Missionary Baptist Church with 10801 S. State Street, and public architectural-history documentation identifies that congregation with the former All Saints church. This supports a probable address/site continuity reading, but no current property record, dated physical survey, or interior/structural assessment was verified; route-level building condition therefore remains unknown. The fate of the earlier 10806 S. Wabash combination church-school building is also unresolved.
summary: All Saints was the Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish organized in Chicago's Roseland/West Pullman area in 1906. A 1908 Lithuanian newspaper account and a visually verified near-period illustrated history both support 1906 formation; August 18, 1907 was the cornerstone milestone, not the founding year. The first combination church-school at 10806 S. Wabash opened in June 1908, and a new church at 10801 S. State was dedicated in June 1960. After Rev. Joseph Lukošius died in 1972, All Saints entered a 1973 territorial consolidation with Holy Rosary, St. Louis de France, and St. Nicholas while retaining the All Saints name; that changed the parish's Lithuanian national character but did not close the institution. The Archdiocese records the parish's end on December 31, 1989 and custody of its records at the Archives and Records Center. Current public sources associate a Baptist congregation with the State Street address and identify it with the former church, but present physical condition is not directly verified; the earlier building's outcome and any parish cemetery remain unresolved.

historicalNarrative.text: All Saints was a distinct Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish in the Archdiocese of Chicago, not the Irish All Saints near Wallace Street or the Polish National Catholic All Saints congregation. A 1908 Lietuva account says local Lithuanian societies decided in 1906 to organize the parish, and a visually verified near-period illustrated Archdiocesan souvenir likewise labels All Saints Lithuanian and founded in 1906 at 10806 Wabash Avenue. These sources resolve the inherited 1906-versus-1907 question: 1906 belongs to parish organization, while 1907 belongs to the church cornerstone.

historicalNarrative.text: The first parish complex was a combination church and school at 10806 South Wabash Avenue. Wolkovich dates the cornerstone blessing to August 18, 1907 and the dedication to June 14, 1908; the Archdiocesan locations register independently places the 1908 church at the southeast corner of 108th and Wabash. The school opened in 1910 under the Sisters of St. Casimir. No evidence reviewed establishes the later fate of this first building after worship moved in 1960.

historicalNarrative.text: A new All Saints church was built at 10801 South State Street. The register guide identifies a May 1959 cornerstone milestone and dedication on June 16, 1960, after which parish worship used the State Street church. The later building did not mark a new parish founding: it was the second worship site of the institution organized in 1906.

historicalNarrative.text: The parish's ethnic status changed before its juridic life ended. Wolkovich says All Saints became territorial soon after Rev. Joseph Lukošius died on July 7, 1972. The Archdiocesan locations register dates a consolidation with Holy Rosary, St. Louis de France, and St. Nicholas to February 23, 1973 and says the resulting parish retained the All Saints name. The dossier therefore treats 1972–1973 as a Lithuanian-national-to-territorial transition, not as closure.

historicalNarrative.text: The institution closed on December 31, 1989. The Archdiocese's 2024 holdings list gives that exact end date, and an Archdiocesan obituary separately describes All Saints on South State as closed in 1989. A public architectural-history page identifies the former church with Universal Community Missionary Baptist Church, while a current nonprofit directory associates that congregation with 10801 South State. Those sources support probable reuse but do not replace a dated property record or physical survey, so building survival, exact continuity, and present condition remain qualified and separate from the Roman Catholic parish's 1989 end.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The inherited 1907 formation reading conflated the church cornerstone with parish organization; contemporary and near-period sources support 1906 formation. Wolkovich's post-1972 territorial status and the 1973 Archdiocesan consolidation are ethnic/administrative milestones, not the parish's end. The institution closed in 1989 while the 1960 building survived in later Baptist use.
gaps: The exact canonical erection instrument, 1973 decree and precise juridic mechanics, fate of the 10806 S. Wabash building, deed and ownership chain for both sites, parcel-level proof joining the current congregation to the former church, complete post-closure property transaction, current structural/interior assessment of the State Street church, comprehensive sacramental-record scope, and any parish cemetery remain unverified.
